title: Digital Banking Must Keep Pace With Changing Customer Expectations
summary: Digital banking customer expectations are evolving fast. Discover how banks can keep pace with more connected, personalized, and intelligent experiences.
body_markdown:
[Digital banking experiences](https://www.forrester.com/report/the-state-of-digital-banking-experiences-2026/RES205563) are evolving as customer behaviors change. Around the world, mobile banking remains customers’ preferred way to interact with their banks, even if online banking and branches continue to play important roles. At the same time, customers are embracing[conversational AI and third-party AI tools](https://www.forrester.com/report/consumers-use-ai-for-personal-finance-but-not-necessarily-from-their-bank/RES201284?ref_search=2881951_1794916967463) like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude and engaging with banks across an expanding ecosystem of[devices, platforms, and channels](https://www.forrester.com/go?objectid=RES181929) .


Customers increasingly expect banking to be easy, connected, personalized, and intelligent, while still providing access to human support and expertise when it matters. To keep pace, banks need to:


### **Provide Convenient, Consistent, And Empathetic Experiences Across Channels**


Banking journeys rarely stay within a single channel or touchpoint. Customers use multiple interaction modes (graphical user interfaces, chat, and voice) and move between digital and human-assisted channels, particularly for more complex journeys. In the UK, for example, 41% of recent mortgage borrowers combined online and offline touchpoints when researching and applying for a mortgage.


Digital convenience does not eliminate the need for people. Customers still value human expertise for complex decisions, financial guidance, and emotionally significant moments. Banks must connect digital and human experiences so customers can move between them easily, without having to repeat themselves or lose context along the way.


### **Help Customers Achieve Their Goals With Proactive And Personalized Support**


Customers increasingly expect banks to do more than help them complete transactions. They want support that reflects their goals, behaviors, and financial circumstances. In fact, 66% of customers say it is important that their provider offers personalized recommendations tailored to their goals, behavior, and financial situation. Customers are also more willing to share personal data when they receive clear value in return, like[better outcomes, lower costs, or more convenient experiences](https://www.forrester.com/go?objectid=res178785) . Banks must use customer context to move beyond generic interactions and deliver timely, relevant support that helps customers make progress toward their financial goals.


### **Meet Customers Wherever They Choose To Engage**


The boundaries of digital banking are expanding beyond bank-owned apps and websites. As customers increasingly use conversational and AI-powered interfaces, leading banks are making services available across a broader ecosystem of channels and platforms. For example,[ICICI Bank’s WhatsApp Banking service](https://www.icici.bank.in/personal-banking/ways-to-bank/mobile-banking/whatsapp-banking) enables customers to access banking services through an interface they already use. Banks must make relevant services available wherever customers choose to engage while maintaining continuity, context, trust, and control across those interactions.


### **Deliver Intelligent Banking Experiences**


The next evolution of digital banking is not simply more digital. It is more intelligent. The most effective experiences are evolving along three dimensions:


- **Assistive experiences** provide timely, relevant, and actionable guidance that helps customers make better financial decisions.
- **Anticipatory experiences** identify emerging needs, risks, and opportunities, from changing financial circumstances and potential fraud to significant life events, and recommend action before customers ask for help.
- **Agentic experiences** move digital and conversational banking beyond answering questions toward completing tasks and acting on customers’ behalf within defined parameters.


[Delivering these future experiences](https://www.forrester.com/report/the-future-of-digital-banking-experiences/RES182388?ref_search=2881951_1794916543061) requires banks to strengthen their data, AI, analytics, and orchestration capabilities so they can understand customer intent, anticipate needs, coordinate interactions, and deliver personalized guidance at scale.


#### **Digital Banking Is Becoming More Human-Centered And Intelligent**


The future of digital banking is not about replacing human interactions with digital ones. It is about combining the strengths of both while using data and AI to make banking more contextual, proactive, and useful.


Banks must move beyond transactional digital experiences toward connected, personalized, and intelligent experiences that help customers achieve better financial outcomes wherever and however they choose to engage.
